_comment: Authoritative publication list.  CSL-JSON, so a reference manager can read
it and Python needs no dependency to parse it.  See docs/adr/006.
Built by reconciling the three lists that previously disagreed: docs/cv.md,
the Zola research page, and the Zotero export at src/pubs.json in the Zola
repository.  scripts/python/reconcile_bibliography.py reproduces that
comparison; docs/adr/006 records what it found.
`issued` is the publication date of the version of record: the print date
where a journal has one, the online date otherwise, to whatever precision
the publisher gives.  `_preprint.arxiv-year` carries the arXiv posting year
where it differs -- Zotero recorded those as `issued`, which is why its
years looked wrong against the other two lists.
`URL` is the published version.  `_arxiv` is the preprint, and the two are
rendered side by side.  An entry that is itself a preprint of another names
it with `_version-of`, which is why one arXiv id may appear on two entries.
`_cv` marks the entries the CV's 'Selected publications' section carries.
It is a curation, not a ranking: the six here are the six the CV listed
before it was generated from this file.  Adding or removing one is a
one-line edit followed by `make publications`.
`_needs_review` marks a field the three sources disagree on and that could
not be settled from them.  Two remain, and both are decisions for a person
rather than facts to look up.  Each note records what the publishers say.
Every entry carrying a DOI or an arXiv identifier has been checked against
the publisher's own record -- Crossref, DataCite or the arXiv API -- by
scripts/python/verify_bibliography.py.  `make publications-verify` repeats
the comparison and reports every difference.  The four entries with neither
identifier are reconciled claims still, and the verifier lists them as
unverifiable rather than passing over them.
